mechanisms.name: Default `rotationPolicy` Never -> Always (Certificate.spec.privateKey.rotationPolicy default, feature gate DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways)
resourcesConsumers: Certificate/mesh-root-ca (platform/pki/base/mesh-root-ca.yaml and its prod overlay patch)
mechanisms.mechanism: No Certificate sets privateKey.rotationPolicy, so all four move from Never to Always; the feature gate is left at its new default (on). Nothing is reissued by the upgrade itself; the policy applies at the next issuance (renewal, manual `cmctl renew`, or a spec change that forces reissue). When mesh-root-ca next renews it gets a new key pair, with a different public key and no overlap or cross-signing, and mesh-ca then signs new leaves with the new key. cert-manager copies the issuer CA cert into each leaf's ca.crt at the time that leaf is issued, and the leaves renew independently of each other and of the root. So a leaf renewed after the root gets the new ca.crt while an unrenewed leaf keeps an old-key cert and an old ca.crt. mTLS between ledger and checkout then fails in both directions (e.g. "unable to get local issuer certificate"). This lasts until both leaves are reissued and self-heals only if pods pick up the new Secrets. Nothing in the repo reissues leaves when the root changes, and pods do not reload on Secret changes. Under 1.17 (Never), a root renewal reused the same key, so old leaves and stale ca.crt kept verifying. Blast radius: mesh-wide failure of ledger and checkout calls in payments production. It is silent until it happens, no manifest diff shows it, and the first root renewal could be months away.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: Nothing in the repo mitigates it. Recommended mitigation: pin `privateKey.rotationPolicy: Never` on mesh-root-ca (base or prod overlay) in Git before, or in the same change as, the version bump. For leaves, either set Never too or accept Always once ledger reload behaviour is understood and tested. Leave the feature gate alone, because disabling it is a temporary escape that disappears in 1.19. Plan a deliberate root CA rotation process (overlapping trust, leaf reissue, pod restart) before ever setting Always on the root.
citedEvidence: upstream/.../upgrading-1.17-1.18.md and release-notes-1.18.md list it as a breaking change; feature-gated (DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways), on by default, not switchable in 1.19

mechanisms.name: Leaf key rotation and nginx / curl behaviour
resourcesConsumers: ledger (nginx, ssl_certificate / ssl_certificate_key from a mounted Secret)
checkout (curl re-reading files on every call)
mechanisms.mechanism: Rated "LOW to MODERATE, mostly a pre-existing weakness". Leaf renewals now also rotate the leaf private key. There is no key or fingerprint pinning and validation is by CA only, so rotation does not break trust by itself. nginx loads the cert and key at start or reload, and the repo has no reloader, sidecar or annotation. After a leaf renewal the running nginx keeps serving the old cert and key, which are consistent, so nothing breaks until the old cert expires (30 days). This was also true on 1.17 and is a pre-existing expiry outage waiting to happen, not something 1.18 introduces. With a rotated key, however, someone relying on a ledger restart to pick up the new Secret will now get a new key too. checkout picks up new material within about 30s, and kubelet's atomic Secret volume swap keeps tls.crt and tls.key consistent. A nginx restart during root rotation would pick up the new ca.crt while checkout might still hold the old one, which makes the section 1 mismatch worse.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: Rotation does not break trust by itself because validation is by CA only and there is no key or fingerprint pinning. The nginx no-reload issue is pre-existing (also true on 1.17).
citedEvidence: No pinning of leaf keys or fingerprints exists anywhere in the repo
ledger nginx `ssl_certificate` / `ssl_certificate_key` read from a mounted Secret
No reloader, sidecar, or annotation in the repo
assumptions: Kubelet swaps the Secret volume atomically, so tls.crt and tls.key stay consistent
missingEvidence: Whether anything outside this repo (a reloader operator, admission mutation) restarts ledger on Secret change
recommendedValidation: Confirm whether anything outside the repo restarts ledger on Secret change; if not, test that a leaf renewal is never picked up by nginx and decide whether to fix that separately
Accept Always on leaves only once ledger reload behaviour is understood and tested

mechanisms.name: `revisionHistoryLimit` default nil -> 1
mechanisms.mechanism: revisionHistoryLimit is not set on any Certificate, so the default applies, and stale CertificateRequest objects are garbage-collected on upgrade. The only loss is history for audit or forensic use.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: No consumer of old CertificateRequests was found (no scripts, policies, or Argo health customisations in the repo). If the org relies on CertificateRequest history as a record of mesh issuance, snapshot it first.

mechanisms.name: ACME / HTTP01 `PathType: Exact`, ACME profiles, Vault `serverName`, DNS01 RBAC split
resourcesConsumers: ClusterRole cert-manager-controller-challenges -> cert-manager-dns01-controller-challenges / cert-manager-http01-controller-challenges, plus matching ClusterRoleBindings
mechanisms.mechanism: The HTTP01 PathType: Exact change (and its ingress-nginx workaround) applies only to ACME HTTP01 with Ingress solvers. The challenges ClusterRole is split into dns01 and http01 roles, with matching ClusterRoleBinding renames, for the same ServiceAccount. Argo prune will delete the old role and binding and create the new ones. GHSA-8rvj-mm4h-c258 concerns direct ACME Challenge resources using ClusterIssuer DNS01 credentials.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: There are no ACME or Vault issuers and no Ingress or Gateway resources. The RBAC split preserves controller permissions, and the prune/create is expected churn, not a breaking change. The advisory lists v1.18.6 and v1.19.5 as affected, so it is not a reason to stay on 1.17, and it is not exploitable here because no ACME issuer exists. Whether anything else in the cluster binds to the old role name is unknown.

mechanisms.name: Rendered chart changes (images/labels, webhook probes, CRD additions, CRD delivery, values, commonName IP-address fix, name-constraints fix)
mechanisms.mechanism: Images and labels move from v1.17.2 to v1.18.0. Webhook probes change from numeric port 6080 to the named port healthcheck. The CRDs gain profile, serverName and signatureAlgorithm fields and iss/ciss short names, with doc-text edits and removal of the AdditionalCertificateOutputFormats doc text. CRDs are delivered through the chart with ServerSideApply. The commonName IP-address and name-constraints fixes ship upstream.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: The probe change is equivalent (containerPort 6080 is named healthcheck). The CRD changes are additive, and no existing field in the repo is removed or retyped. CRDs are kept on uninstall (keep: true). values.yaml uses only keys that still exist in 1.18.0. The commonName and name-constraints fixes don't apply, because the commonNames are DNS names and NameConstraints is not enabled.
